examples: coffee price rises -> demand for tea rises (substitutes)
income rises -> fewer bus rides (inferior good)
lines: Demand: the quantity of a good buyers are willing and able to buy at each price
Law of demand: as price rises, quantity demanded falls (other things equal)
Demand shifters: income, tastes, prices of related goods, expectations
Normal good: demand rises when income rises
Inferior good: demand falls when income rises
Supply: the quantity sellers are willing and able to sell at each price
Law of supply: as price rises, quantity supplied rises
Equilibrium: the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
Shortage: quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, below the equilibrium price
Surplus: quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, above the equilibrium price
e.g. coffee price rises -> demand for tea rises (substitutes)
e.g. income rises -> fewer bus rides (inferior good)
